subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add Mission Control workspace-wide editing and/or host system filesystem browsing beyond the current bootstrap-file editor and read-only workspace browser?
rationale: The remaining request changes which workspace and host files operator clients can read or mutate, and current main deliberately keeps edits allowlisted while only approving a bounded read-only workspace slice.

options.title: Workspace-Only First
options.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.list/get` surface as the safe base, settle workspace mutation scope in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368, and defer system filesystem browsing.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap Editing Only
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing limited to core bootstrap files while allowing only the already-approved read-only workspace browsing surfaces.

options.title: Design System Scope Separately
options.body: Create a separate host-filesystem design with explicit operator opt-in, authorization, auditing, limits, and non-destructive defaults.

recommendation.title: Workspace-Only First
recommendation.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.list/get` surface as the safe base, settle workspace mutation scope in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61368, and defer system filesystem browsing.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the current read-only workspace API and mobile browser slice, which is the closest approved boundary for this decision.
